original_failure.observed_error: interrupted idle turn should expose its recovery epoch: Elapsed(())
original_failure.limitations: The failure proves that the epoch was not observed in the original five-second budget. It does not contain a per-event trace proving when response.created crossed the owner gate.

source_causal_chain.fact: The original fixture releases response.created immediately and gates only response.completed, then interrupts after the first physical request and historical durable Ready assertions.
The first successfully received ResponseEvent closes recovery authority before matching the event; ResponseEvent::Created is included.
The same-owner first-output gate calls ensure_turn_recovery_unready while the exact task and authority are still attached.
An interrupted recovery seed requires an eligible model turn, durable Ready state, ready atomic, and the recorded replay/fingerprint/generation. An old Ready entry alone is insufficient.

The server records and notifies the physical request before awaiting any chunk gate. Its bare SSE headers do not contain model or rate-limit event metadata. Dropping the release sender makes the gated chunk return without writing provider event bytes.

inference: The original fixture permits response.created to invalidate Ready before its Interrupt, contrary to this test's intended pre-output recovery scenario. Relocating the same gate before the first event eliminates that fixture interleaving without weakening the production recovery boundary.
change: Move the existing first_response_gate from response.completed to response.created. Keep the event bodies and order, sender, interrupt, sender drop, and every subsequent recovery assertion identical.

The original test count and all original assertion/panic/expect expressions, in their original order.
